context_review.learning_area_reason: The subject supports water systems, sustainability, resourcefulness, practical self-reliance and household resilience while transferring naturally into other RRA learning areas.

conflicts_found: Performance claims for slow-sand filtration vary by design, maturity, organism, source water, operation and study setting.
Online language frequently treats ordinary charcoal and activated carbon as interchangeable; the project rejects that simplification.
unresolved_questions: The live Academy website should be re-checked when the browsing tool can retrieve it.

concept.learning_outcome: Explain the distinct jobs in water treatment, identify why treatment must match the contaminant, safely demonstrate physical filtration, and transfer the diagnosis-before-prescription principle into other areas of life.
concept.central_question: What are you actually trying to remove?
major_principles: Clear water is not automatically safe water.
Water treatment is a system, not a magic ingredient.
Filtration and disinfection are not the same thing.
Activated carbon and ordinary charcoal are not the same thing.
Source protection can matter more than downstream treatment.
Maintenance and safe storage affect performance.
Do not claim more than the evidence proves.
concept.historical_or_lost_knowledge_angle: Historical rural households had to understand the entire source-to-storage water system; early farm guidance already warned that filtration was not a guarantee of drinking-water safety.
concept.current_use_angle: Use the framework to understand wells, rainwater, emergencies, household filters, source protection, contaminant-specific treatment and filter marketing.
concept.transfer_the_principle_summary: Diagnose before prescribing. Match the solution to the actual problem; use layered defenses; verify what changed.

pricing.role: paid core field guide with free public sample
